subject: Priority One: Latency & Error Surge Impacting Checkout - Mobilization
messages:
From: Alex Chen <alex.chen@horizonretail.com>
To: vanessa_ortiz@redwood.ai
Cc: jordan.miles@horizonretail.com
Date: Wed, 20 May 2026 08:12:00 -0700
Subject: Significant latency + 5xx spike on checkout (urgent)

Vanessa / Redwood team —

We just saw a large increase in latency across our checkout calls to your inference API starting ~07:45 PDT. Error rates (5xx) jumped from ~0.2% to ~6% and median p95 latency has moved from ~150ms to ~1.2s. This is causing timeouts in our synchronous checkout flow and customer drop-off.

Impact: ~15% failed checkouts on US region, live traffic is affected. We are throttling some traffic but need Redwood to prioritize.

Can you confirm you have an incident and what the initial triage shows? We need an ETA for a mitigation path; our ops and execs are standing by.

Attached: quick logs and a short sample of failed request IDs.

— Alex
Alex Chen
CTO, Horizon Retail
alex.chen@horizonretail.com
From: vanessa_ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.ai>
To: alex.chen@horizonretail.com, jordan.miles@horizonretail.com
Cc: marcus_lin@redwood.ai, laura_bennett@redwood.ai, rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai
Date: Wed, 20 May 2026 08:22:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Significant latency + 5xx spike on checkout (urgent)

Alex — thank you for the heads up and the samples. This is priority one for us.

Immediate plan: assemble a cross-functional response (SRE + Prod + CS). Marcus, Laura, Rishi — please join a short war-room at 08:30 PDT to triage and stand up mitigations.

What we will do in first 30 minutes:
- Confirm scope and rollback/route options
- Check capacity and fallbacks (model variants, dedicated pool routing)
- Provide a customer-facing interim status within 30 minutes

Alex/Jordan, we will keep this thread for email summaries and also post to the incident Slack channel (link attached). I attached the initial error summary you sent for the record.

Owners: Marcus (technical lead), Laura (customer comms), Rishi (product/rollback decisions).

— Vanessa Ortiz
Head of Sales Engineering, Redwood Inference
vanessa_ortiz@redwood.ai

From: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.ai>
To: vanessa_ortiz@redwood.ai, laura_bennett@redwood.ai, rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai
Cc: alex.chen@horizonretail.com, jordan.miles@horizonretail.com
Date: Wed, 20 May 2026 08:33:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Significant latency + 5xx spike on checkout (urgent)

Quick triage notes from the 08:30 standup:
- Observed: p95 latency and 5xx both spiked starting 07:42 PDT in us-west region for Horizon routing.
- Root signals: elevated KV cache eviction rates -> higher cold KV lookups; continuous batching backlog on a subset of pods; one autoscale event hit max burst limit around 07:50.
- Error pattern: 502/504 originating in the runtime IPC layer when batch assembly timed out.

Immediate mitigations in flight:
1) Bump dedicated pool burst capacity for Horizon routing (applied 08:31) — expected to reduce queuing within 2–5 mins.
2) Enable fallback model variant (smaller, quantized) for non-critical checkout paths to drop p95 — rolling 08:34–08:40.
3) Increase per-pod request timeouts to avoid IPC cascades; this is a protective change.

Metrics & links: Grafana shortlink (ops): https://grafana.redwood.internal/d/ops/latency?orgId=1&from=now-1h  — attaching a screenshot.

I will monitor and post updates every 10 minutes.

— Marcus
Marcus Lin
SRE Lead, Redwood Inference
marcus_lin@redwood.ai

Thanks for the patience. For external comms we recommend a short, candid status update you can share with your stakeholders:

"We are working with Redwood Inference to mitigate an elevated latency and error rate impacting checkout. laura_bennett@redwood.ai
From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai>
To: vanessa_ortiz@redwood.ai, marcus_lin@redwood.ai, laura_bennett@redwood.ai
Cc: alex.chen@horizonretail.com, jordan.miles@horizonretail.com
Date: Wed, 20 May 2026 09:02:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Significant latency + 5xx spike on checkout (urgent)

Update from product side after reviewing options:
- Rollback option: revert recent routing policy change that increased request multiplexing for Horizon bundle (low-risk) — ready to rollback at 09:10 if metrics don't improve.
- Safer opt: route Horizon traffic to a dedicated, warmed pool (costly but immediate). Marcus has already increased burst capacity; next step is to pin critical checkout routes to warmed instances for 30 minutes.
- Post-mitigation: we'll run a canary for 15 minutes then gradually release.

Estimate: if fallback + burst hold, we should see p95 return under 300ms within 20–30 minutes. If not, rollback at 09:10 will be executed (estimated additional improvement 20–40%).

Action items assigned: Marcus (monitor + execute rollback if needed), Laura (finalize customer-facing update), Vanessa (exec comms & escalation).

— Rishi Malhotra
VP Product, Redwood Inference
rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai

Thanks — quick clarification: this is actively impacting live checkout, not a subset. We need a firm ETA to share with ops and the on-call execs. Can you confirm whether the fallback routing is safe for payment verification flows? We cannot degrade fraud scoring accuracy at checkout.

If fallback is not safe for payments, prioritize routing critical traffic to warmed dedicated instances and we will tolerate a temporary increase in cost. Please confirm in 15 minutes.

— Jordan

From: vanessa_ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.ai>

Date: Wed, 20 May 2026 15:45:00 -0700
Subject: Executive summary — Horizon Checkout Incident (Status & Next Steps)

Leads & Execs — FYI and high level summary of the incident impacting Horizon Retail (priority one).

Timeline:
- 07:42 PDT: Latency and 5xx increase detected for Horizon routing.
- 08:31–08:40: Burst capacity increased; fallback model variant enabled for non-payment paths.
- 09:10: Rollback of recent multiplexing policy staged (not required yet).

Current status (15:45 PDT):
- Checkout success rate regained to ~97% (from 85% at peak). p95 latency stabilized ~320ms.
- Customer agreed to dedicated warmed pool for critical checkout routes for next 2 hours to ensure stability.
- Root cause likely a combination of cache pressure and an unexpected autoscale ceiling on specific pod group; full RCA in progress.

Open actions:
- Marcus: finish post-incident logs and IPC traces, publish RCA draft by EOD.
- Rishi: propose policy change to avoid single-burst ceilings; coordinate with infra roadmap.
- Laura: send final customer incident summary and credits proposal (if requested).
- Ops: review autoscale config for similar bundles across customers.

Customer sentiment: Horizon ops and execs are satisfied with the mitigation; they requested an EOD note and a 1:1 review tomorrow.

I will follow up with the RCA and a timeline for permanent mitigations.

— Vanessa Ortiz
Head of Sales Engineering, Redwood Inference
